title: compact-fit-allocator-and-batched-kv-rebalance-to-reduce-eviction-latency
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Introduce a compact-fit slab allocator for KV cache and tenant-aware batched rebalance that reduces eviction tail latency and fragmentation. Backwards-compatible runtime changes; no customer API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed multi-tenant KV cache tail latency spikes under bursty traffic when fragmentation and reactive spillover combined with synchronous eviction caused blocking IO and long token latency. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) a compact-fit allocator for the KV resident store that reduces internal fragmentation and coalesces free spans with minimal stop-the-world work, and (2) a tenant-aware, batched rebalance/eviction planner that groups eviction work into short jobs aligned with the runtime's continuous-batching windows to avoid per-request eviction stalls. The goal is to reduce eviction-induced latency spikes and lower background spill IO while keeping steady-state memory residency efficient.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Implemented compact-fit allocator with lightweight freelist buckets and adjacent-span coalescing on free; minimizes per-allocation metadata and supports fast-fit placement for common slab sizes.
- Added periodic, tenant-scoped rebalance which collects fragmentation and residency metrics and issues eviction/relocation as batched jobs to the runtime scheduler; these jobs are sized to fit the continuous-batching latency budget.
- Evictor changes: a soft-quarantine window for recently demoted pages prevents immediate re-eviction thrashing; spillback rate limiting is tenant-scoped to avoid noisy-neighbor IO storms.
- Kernel hinting: allocator exposes hot/cold classification metadata that can be consumed by the kernel selection layer to prefer compact-friendly kernels for contiguous memory ranges.
- Observability: added fragmentation_score, rebalance_jobs_active, last_spill_size_bytes, and tenant_spillback_rate metrics; dashboards updated in docs/observability.
- Tests: unit tests for allocator correctness, integration tests that simulate bursty workloads with mixed-tenancy, and a perf microbenchmark showing reduced max eviction pause.

Design notes and trade-offs: 
- Compact-fit allocator vs. full compaction: we avoided heavy-moving compaction (which would require pointer rewrites across many layers) by doing coalescing on free and opportunistic relocation during rebalance jobs. That reduces latency impact while still yielding significantly lower fragmentation for tenant workloads with many short-lived allocations.
- Batched rebalance sizing: rebalance jobs are bounded by the runtime's continuous-batching latency budget (configurable). By packing eviction/relocation into those short jobs we amortize work without violating token-latency SLOs. We allow a tenant override for aggressive reclaim in Dedicated tiers.
- Spillback throttling: rate limiting is tenant-scoped; conservative defaults prevent cross-tenant amplification but enterprise customers can tune via Dedicated policies.

CI and validation summary:
- CI pipeline: build -> unit tests -> integration (in-memory) -> benchmark-lab perf run (nightly) -> lint
- First CI run: build passed, unit tests passed, integration showed a flaky eviction_pause test (investigated)
- Second CI run: fixed test, all checks passed. Benchmark-lab nightly run showed a 22% reduction in 99.9th-percentile eviction pause on the mixed-tenancy scenario; median allocation throughput unchanged.

Observability and ops guidance:
- New metrics added with dashboards in docs/observability/kv-fragmentation.md. Operations should watch fragmentation_score per-tenant and rebalance_jobs_active; if tenant_spillback_rate is high, consider increasing tenant spillback window or enabling Dedicated tenant aggressive reclaim.
- Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag kv_compact_fit_enabled (off by default). Rollout sequence: enable in canary, monitor fragmentation and eviction tail, ramp to 100% when stable. Canary notes included in docs.

Backward compatibility and migration: No changes to public APIs. Data layout for on-disk spill files unchanged. Runtime flag controls behavior; admins can disable if necessary.
